problem_summary.summary: Compress a sorted, unique integer array into the smallest list of consecutive ranges that cover exactly its values.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: nums, sorted ascending with no duplicates. Return strings formatted as a single integer or start->end.
constraints: nums is sorted and contains unique values

brute_force.explanation: For each range start, walk forward while each next number is exactly one larger. Store all numbers in that run temporarily, then format its first and last values.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A run ends precisely at the first missing integer. Since the input is sorted and unique, each maximal run is disjoint from the next and together the runs contain every input value exactly once.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) time, where n is nums.length; each value is visited once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the temporary run, excluding the returned strings.

optimized.explanation: Track only the first and last indices of each consecutive run, then format the endpoints directly without storing the run's values.
optimized.correctness_idea: The endpoint advances exactly while adjacent input values differ by one. At the first gap, those endpoints describe one maximal range; continuing at the next index covers the remaining disjoint runs.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) time; the scan visits each array position once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space beyond the O(r) returned range strings, where r is the number of ranges.

steps.action: Close and emit the first range; begin the next run at index 2.
Advance end to index 4 and emit the complete range.
Format the equal endpoints as one number.

edge_cases.handling: The loop does not run and an empty list is returned.
A run with equal start and end is emitted as one integer.
Adjacency is checked after widening to long, avoiding overflow at Integer.MAX_VALUE.
